# Rendering an In-World Text at a specific onscreen position

Source: [9496](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/9496); edited 2026-08-20. Evidence: archived documentation.

Not independently verified in the current game. An article edit date is not a behavioral test date.

<a id="wiki-9496-n1"></a>

- Documented screen-anchored IWT techniques offer placement/size control and post-match visibility; tradeoffs include FOV displacement, newline alignment and lower readability than HUD headers.

<a id="wiki-9496-n2"></a>

- Screen coordinates use origin at crosshair, positive X right and positive Y up. Recommended first-person bounds +/-2.5 X and +/-1.25 Y assume minimum FOV and 16:9, not arbitrary displays.

<a id="wiki-9496-n3"></a>

- Four variants cover first-person versus custom-camera projection and per-player Event Player versus one global Local Player text.

<a id="wiki-9496-n4"></a>

- Local Player variants must run in a Global rule and save text entities, but source says spectators cannot see them as of patch 1.59. Per-player camera variant supports spectators.

<a id="wiki-9496-n5"></a>

- Start Camera fixes user-configured FOV at approximately 102.5 degrees, but hero abilities such as Ball roll/Soldier sprint can still alter FOV and displace the text.

<a id="wiki-9496-n6"></a>

- All variants use Update Every Frame on position and require position reevaluation; freeze only selected X/Y subexpressions with Evaluate Once.

<a id="wiki-9496-n7"></a>

- Projection places text on a plane from eye position plus right/up/facing components. Custom-camera right axis comes from a cross product; upward basis derives from facing angles with vertical angle minus 90.

<a id="wiki-9496-n8"></a>

- Do Not Clip prevents map geometry/viewmodel occlusion. Constants 100,3,0.2 are trial-and-error; distant placement reduces camera sway but can exceed world bounds and require retuning scale/offset.

<a id="wiki-9496-n9"></a>

- Progress-bar versions are included; extensions to icons/effects are suggested, with effects kept closer and possible rotation while the player turns.

Source limitations:

- Header August 2026 coexists with patch-1.59 spectator claims; behavioral validity needs separate verification.

- Intro says progress-bar/icon technique not properly tested, although progress-bar examples were later included; distinguish examples from validated compatibility.

- Local text code uses Visible Never spectator setting while local progress-bar code uses Default Visibility; reconcile before promising spectator behavior.

- No assessment of arbitrary aspect ratios, edge views, third-person transitions or world-boundary behavior supplied.
